records.heading: Introductory largest-value program on FORTRAN coding sheet (visual transcription)
records.context: Manual visual transcription from original PDF physical page 9 (printed page 7), pypdfium2 rendered image. Appended reading aid for the original code sheet; base OCR retained separately.
records.notes: Code-sheet layout normalized to plain text: C occupies column 1; X is visible in the CONTINUATION column on the second comment line. The header identifies C FOR COMMENT, STATEMENT NUMBER (columns 1-5), CONTINUATION (6), FORTRAN STATEMENT (7-72), and IDENTIFICATION (73-80).

records.context: Physical page 10, printed page 8. The manual distinguishes statement numbers, C-marked ignored cards, arbitrary identification columns, statement columns, and blank spacing, then identifies the actual input medium.
records.notes: The reading text misextracts the exponent in line 2 as 2'5; the original shows 2 to the power 15 (=32768). Minor OCR in line 13 reads iliitial for initial. Core comment-card rule at lines 8-10 was visually verified.

records.heading: Complete largest-value program: purpose and input explanation
records.context: Physical page 48, printed page 46. The manual revisits the chapter 1 program, now complete with the same two opening comment cards. The passage gives its purpose, input size/format and first executed statement.
records.notes: The original code sheet lies between lines 10 and 11. Reading-text lines 21-72 mix form rules with damaged code and are not selected as faithful code; the original specimen is separately transcribed. Explanation continues on physical page 49.

records.heading: Complete largest-value program on FORTRAN coding sheet (visual transcription)
records.context: Manual visual transcription from original PDF physical page 48 (printed page 46), pypdfium2 rendered image. Appended reading aid for the original code sheet; base OCR retained separately.

records.heading: Complete largest-value program: control flow, output and frequency assumptions

records.notes: Runtime Hollerith output text is retained as context for this specimen, not relabeled as a source comment. OCR confuses I/1 in places and line 9 damages the comparison sign; visual source controls interpretation. Line 30 flattens the octal subscript on 77777.
